items.detail: 메타의 최고AI책임자(CAIO)와 오픈AI 핵심 연구진이 잇달아 초지능의 위험성을 경고하며 개발 속도를 조절할 구체적인 방안까지 제시하고 있습니다. 단순한 위험 경고를 넘어 개발 제한 기준과 인간의 통제권을 유지할 방법을 제안하기 시작하면서, 미국 정치권의 AI 안전 규제 논의에도 영향을 미칠지 주목됩니다. 올여름부터 다리오 아모데이 앤트로픽 CEO와 샘 알트먼 오픈AI CEO 등은 2027년이면 AI가 스스로 성능을 높이는 '재귀적 자기 개선(RSI)'을 통해 지능 폭발이 시작될 수 있다는 전망을 내놓으며 첨단 모델의 개발 속도 조절을 제안했습니다. 여기에 최근에는 AI의 수학·과학 연구 성과 등을 근거로 위험을 진단하고, 발전 속도를 제한할 기준과 안전 조치까지 제시하는 단계로 바뀌고 있습니다. 알렉산더 왕 메타 CAIO는 22일(현지시간) '초지능이 오고 있다'라는 에세이에서 앞으로 1년 동안 인류의 선택이 미래를 결정할 것이라고 경고했습니다. 그는 AI 발전의 주된 제약이 더 이상 지능이 아니라 전문 지식과 인프라, 실험 환경이라고 주장했습니다. 이런 조건이 갖춰지면 AI가 연구와 실험을 자동화해 인간을 능가하는 속도로 성능을 높일 수 있다는 것입니다. 왕 CAIO는 초지능의 등장을 불가피한 일로 받아들이는 업계의 인식을 비판하며, 인간이 사회의 주도권을 AI에 넘겨서는 안 된다고 강조했습니다. 특히 AI 안전과 보안 기술을 강화하는 데 그치지 않고 업계 전체가 현재의 개발 방식과는 다른 선택을 해야 한다고 촉구했습니다. 구체적인 규제 기준을 제시하지는 않았지만, 개발 방향 자체를 재검토해야 한다는 주장입니다. 23일에는 보아즈 바라크 오픈AI 연구원이 인간의 주도권을 유지하기 위한 방안을 제시했습니다. AI가 인간의 목표와 가치에 부합하도록 만드는 '정렬(Alignment)'에 성공하더라도 인간의 통제권을 유지하는 문제는 별개라고 지적했습니다. 그는 AI를 활용해 인간의 판단과 감독 능력을 높이는 동시에, AI 발전 속도가 인간의 통제 능력을 앞지르지 않도록 제한해야 한다고 주장했습니다. AI의 지능 자체에 상한선을 두기보다는 발전 속도를 조절하자는 것입니다. 이를 위해 기술적인 안전장치와 정부 규제, 국제 협력이 필요하다고 제안했습니다. 알트먼 CEO도 이 글을 공개적으로 지지했습니다. 앞서 야쿠브 파초키 오픈AI 수석과학자는 더 구체적인 개발 제한 기준을 제시했습니다. AI가 다음 단어를 얼마나 정확하게 예측하는지를 나타내는 '퍼플렉시티(Perplexity)' 등을 공통 지표로 삼아 기업들이 개발 한도를 정하고, AI의 행동을 이해하고 감시하는 기술이 일정 수준에 도달하기 전에는 이를 넘지 않도록 하자는 것입니다. 업계가 합의할 수 있는 측정 기준과 개발 재개 조건까지 제안했다는 점에서 주목됩니다. 폴 크리스티아노 오픈AI 재단 이사도 향후 1년 안에 AI가 인간의 통제를 벗어나 재앙을 일으킬 위험을 약 10%로 평가하며 개발 중단을 촉구했습니다. 특히 모든 AI 연구가 아니라 사전학습과 강화학습의 효율 개선, 새로운 모델 구조 개발 등 핵심 성능을 높이는 연구를 일시 중단하고, 모델 가중치와 연구 기밀을 보호할 보안 체계부터 마련해야 한다고 주장했습니다. 과거에는 초지능의 등장 시점과 위험성을 경고하는 데 집중했다면, 이제는 어떤 연구를 중단하고 어떤 기준을 충족해야 개발을 계속할 수 있는지까지 논의하고 있습니다. 단순한 경고를 넘어 실제 규제에 활용할 수 있는 방안을 제시하기 시작한 것입니다. 그러나 이런 경고에도 보안 문제에 따른 일시적인 훈련 중단을 제외하면 AI 기업들이 전반적인 개발 경쟁의 속도를 늦춘 징후는 거의 없습니다. 경쟁사들이 개발을 계속하는 상황에서 어느 한 기업만 속도를 늦추기는 어렵기 때문입니다. 내부 전문가들의 경고가 계속되는 것은 업계 스스로 해결하기 어려운 문제에 외부의 개입이 필요하다는 메시지로도 읽힙니다. 실제로 미국 정치권에서도 AI 안전 규제를 강화할 여건이 조성되고 있습니다. 중간선거에서 승리한 민주당은 내년 의회에서 첨단 AI 모델의 독립적인 안전성 평가와 기업 책임을 강화하는 법안을 추진할 계획입니다. 공화당에서도 AI 안전 규제에 동의하는 의원들이 있어 초당적인 논의가 진행되고 있습니다. 주요 AI 개발사 내부의 경고는 정치권이 규제 정책을 마련하는 데도 영향을 미칠 수 있습니다. 지난 10월 영국 의회는 청문회에서 알트먼과 아모데이 등 주요 AI 기업 CEO들의 과거 위험 경고를 인용하며 각 기업의 정책 담당자들에게 안전성을 추궁했습니다. 당시 앤트로픽의 정책 책임자는 기업들의 자발적인 약속만으로는 충분하지 않다며 정부 차원의 구속력 있는 규제가 필요하다고 답했습니다. 미국에서도 지난 8월 민주당 하원의원들이 AI 에이전트의 외부 시스템 무단 침투 등 통제 이탈 사례를 근거로 오픈AI와 앤트로픽에 해명을 요구했습니다. 9월에는 공화당과 민주당 상원의원들이 각각 AI 연구진의 위험 경고 등을 인용하며 오픈AI에 관련 정보 공개와 안전성 검증을 요구했습니다. 개발자들의 공개 발언이 이미 정치권의 기업 감독에 활용되고 있는 것입니다. AI 업계가 스스로 개발 경쟁을 멈추기 어려운 상황에서 내부 전문가들이 자신들에게 적용될 규제의 방향까지 제시하고 있는 셈입니다. 미국 정치권이 이런 제안들을 어떻게 받아들이고 실제 입법과 감독에 반영할지 주목됩니다. 이어 23일 주요 뉴스입니다. ■ 황 복귀에 엔비디아 직원들 환호…머스크·알트먼도 환영 젠슨 황이 엔비디아 CEO로 복귀하자 수백명의 직원이 본사에 모여 환호했으며, 일론 머스크와 샘 알트먼 등 실리콘밸리 주요 인사들도 환영의 뜻을 밝혔습니다. 황 CEO는 직원들에게 다시 기회를 준 것에 감사하며 두 번째에는 더 나은 CEO가 되겠다고 약속했습니다. ■ '네온'이 3주 만에 '카본'을 추월한 이유…구글 "3개 세대 동시 개발" 구글은 '제미나이 4 네온'이 3주 만에 '카본'의 성능을 넘어선 비결로 3개 세대의 모델을 동시에 개발하고 연구 성과를 지속적으로 반영하는 방식을 소개했습니다. 최근 오픈AI와 앤트로픽의 모델 출시 속도도 빨라지고 있어, 비슷한 병렬 개발 체계를

items.title: Working with AI
items.detail: Nathan Wilmers, Maxim Massenkoff, Peter McCrory Summary How are businesses across the economy adopting AI? What bottlenecks and challenges have they faced? How can employers reorganize human expertise around increasingly capable models? To understand businesses’ experiences better, we conducted 66 interviews with 58 of Anthropic’s enterprise customers. We found: - Sources of AI value. Companies are deploying AI across a dizzying range of knowledge work tasks. In particular, they are increasingly using coding agents to bring software capabilities to nontechnical roles. Interviewees report that most uses of AI add value by increasing their output, rather than by cutting costs. They attribute this both to AI accelerating existing work and to its role in introducing novel product and service improvements. - Impact on employment. Across our interviews, we saw very few examples of domestic layoffs that were driven by AI automation. Although some companies reported hiring more due to AI, most companies reported hiring less due to AI. Many also reported reducing their use of contractors, particularly offshore ones. These reported cuts could be an early warning of job disruption in the international business services industry. - Bottlenecks. Companies reported a range of bottlenecks, including experts resisting AI deployment and tasks that are not accelerated by AI. As coding speeds up, for example, other tasks—like code review, sales, and strategic decision-making—increasingly need to keep pace. - Limits to top-down and bottom-up approaches. Many companies approach AI by identifying a workflow to automate and rolling out a top-down solution. This approach can lead to job insecurity, fears of workplace surveillance, and resistance from the experts needed to set up an effective and durable workflow. Companies that distribute AI tools and wait for bottom-up adoption see some valuable AI use but face bottlenecks from unequal adoption and single-task AI implementations. - Reorganizing for AI. Interviewees described the highest-value uses as involving meaningful reorganization. Some companies are broadening their employees’ roles to ensure individuals can take ownership over whole workflows, and are redeploying employees to the “bottleneck” tasks that AI models cannot do. Some also seek to empower employees by building out infrastructure to support nondeveloper coding and by providing broad-based internal access to business data. These companies are reorganizing to take advantage of ongoing model capability improvements rather than settling on a fixed approach that assumes AI tools will remain as powerful as they are today. Introduction The use of LLMs has exploded across the economy. How are human organizations reshaping around these strange new collaborators? Consider an employee at a midsize law firm that we spoke to. items.detail: 젠슨 황 엔비디아 CEO가 복귀 후 첫 전 직원회의에서 회사 행동 강령 위반을 인정하고 사과했으며, 심리 치료와 경영 방식 개선 등 재발 방지 대책을 공개했다. 또 자신이 특별 대우를 받거나 도널드 트럼프 미국 대통령의 압력으로 복귀한 것이 아니라 이사회의 판단에 따른 결정이었다고 강조했다. 월스트리트저널(WSJ)과 로이터 등은 24일(현지시간) 황 CEO가 미국 캘리포니아주 산타클라라 본사에서 약 한 시간 동안 전 직원회의를 열고 자신의 행동과 복귀 과정에 대해 설명했다고 보도했다. 황 CEO는 자신이 회사 행동 강령을 위반했으며 "끔찍한 실수를 저질렀다"라고 인정했다. 아내와 가족에게도 사과했으며, 다시 기회를 얻은 것에 감사한다고 밝혔다. 또 매일 한 시간 반씩 심리 치료를 받고 있으며, 많은 도움이 되고 있다고 말했다. 자신의 경영 방식에도 문제가 있었다고 인정했다. 업무에 대한 열정과 높은 요구 수준이 직원들의 성과를 높이는 데 도움이 되지만, 지나치면 상대방에게 상처를 주고 자신감을 떨어뜨릴 수 있다는 것이다. 이를 개선하기 위해 함께 일하는 직원들로부터 매달 의견을 수렴하는 '360도 다면 평가'를 받겠다고 약속했다. 여성 직원들이 안전하게 일할 수 있는 근무 환경을 보장하기 위해 노력하겠다는 입장도 밝혔다. 특히 자신의 복귀 결정이 정당한 절차를 거쳤다는 점을 강조했다. 자신이 법 위에 있는 특별한 존재는 아니라며, 행동 강령 위반이 용납될 수는 없지만 모든 위반 행위가 해고로 이어지는 것은 아니라고 설명했다. 구체적인 사실과 상황에 따라 판단해야 한다는 것이다. 트럼프 대통령의 압력으로 이사회가 자신을 복귀시켰다는 주장도 부인했다. 앞서 트럼프 대통령은 CNBC 인터뷰에서 이사회에 직접 연락해 복귀를 설득했으며, 자신의 개입이 중요한 역할을 했다고 밝힌 바 있다. 이에 대해 황 CEO는 이사회가 관련 사실을 검토하고 자신이 국가안보에 위협이 되지 않는다고 판단해 복귀를 결정했다고 설명했다. 미국 정부가 관련 정보를 신속하게 제공한 것에 대해서는 감사의 뜻을 전했다. 또 엔비디아는 특정 정당을 지지하는 기업이 아니며, 어느 행정부가 집권하든 협력할 것이라고 강조했다. 이는 복귀 결정 과정에서 엔비디아 이사회의 독립성이 쟁점으로 떠오른 것과 관련이 있다. 기업 지배구조 전문가들은 자체 조사가 끝나기도 전에 이사회가 복귀를 결정한 데 대해 문제를 제기하고 있다. 미국 민주당 의원들도 트럼프 행정부가 민간 기업의 경영진 인사에 개입한 경위까지 조사하겠다는 입장이다. 이날 회의에서 직원들의 질문을 받지는 않았다. 한편, 전날 그의 복귀 소식에 31.5% 급등했던 엔비디아 주가는 이날 장중 7% 이상 하락했다. 경영 공백은 해소됐지만, 지배구조 문제와 AI 칩의 중국 우회 공급 의혹 등을 둘러싼 각종 조사는 여전히 진행 중이다. 황 CEO는 다음 달 3일 미국 상원 공개 청문회에 출석할 예정이다. 임대준 기자 ydj@aitimes.com

items.title: Tidal bans AI-generated music
items.detail: The music streaming service Tidal said Tuesday that it would ban tracks it believes are completely AI-generated starting next month, a move its leader believes “will resonate with both artists and listeners alike.” The service will remove the AI tracks starting Dec. 9, making Tidal the first music streaming platform to ban AI music entirely. It comes nearly five months after Tidal said it would demonetize any AI-powered song, force those artists to label their tracks as either AI-generated or AI-assisted and ban AI songs that were associated with “fraudulent activity,” a category that includes songs impersonating established artists and efforts to “deceive listeners.” “But that’s enough, as 43% of tracks distributed to us in the last 90 days have been detected as AI-generated. Something more drastic needs to be done,” wrote Robert Andersen, the Tidal Lead at parent company Block, in an X thread on Tuesday. “We’ll begin removing all wholly AI-generated tracks from our catalog, and you’ll see them completely gone by the beginning of the year.” Andersen said that 96% of all AI-generated songs receive zero plays. The move will cleave the platform of 29 million tracks, he added, and have it reject between 80,000 to 85,000 songs a day. “We encourage our peers to follow suit,” he wrote. The move comes as competitors such as Spotify and Apple Music continue to test approaches to combat the rise of AI-generated tracks proliferating on their platforms, many of which the services have labeled some version of “slop” or “spam.” Apple Music said it would also begin labeling AI-generated or AI-assisted tracks on its platform, while Spotify said it would label artists it deemed AI creations as an “AI Persona.” Spotify said in a blog post last month it also removed 50 million slop or spam tracks from users’ recommendations this year, which came after it removed 75 million of those songs from its catalog entirely. The revelation came among a number of updates regarding Spotify’s efforts to combat AI spam. “This work isn’t finished,” Spotify added. “AI moves fast, and bad actors adapt just as fast. But as AI makes music more abundant, we believe listeners will value human artistry even more. Our job is to make Spotify the place they find it.”

items.title: Jensen Huang still thinks a succession plan creates unnecessary hierarchy
items.title_ko: Jensen Huang still thinks a succession plan creates unnecessary hierarchy
items.summary: It's a remarkable stance for a company that spent the last two weeks finding out what happens without its founder.
items.detail: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang kicked off his return to the chipmaker he co-founded by holding an all-hands meeting that covered remorse, therapy, and even the company’s code of conduct, according to accounts from multiple insiders who spoke to the media. The topic of succession planning also came up — a particularly sticky issue seen as a key risk at Nvidia. Huang reportedly told staff that Nvidia doesn’t require succession planning because of its unique business model, CNBC reported, citing an unnamed source who was present. Surprisingly, given the events of the last two weeks, Huang argued that a succession plan would create unnecessary hierarchy. Investors and analysts saw the issue differently earlier this month, when Huang resigned as CEO following his admission that he had extramarital affairs with at least two people, including one whom the U.S. government suspects of being a Chinese spy. Nvidia is a flat organization, unlike other large corporations that have a swath of C-suite executives and multiple layers of management. Huang sits at the top and says he has about 60 direct reports. Nvidia has just five executive officers running the show, including Huang. The other four are CFO Colette Kress, who was interim CEO for 12 days; Ajay Puri, who heads worldwide field operations; Debora Shoquist, executive vice president of operations; and Timothy Teter, executive vice president and general counsel, according to the company’s regulatory filings. Huang has previously defended the company’s structure in numerous interviews, including one in March with podcaster Lex Fridman. “When you’re designing a company, you should first think about what is it that you want the company to produce,” Huang said in the interview. “You know, I see a lot of companies’ organization charts, and they all look the same. Hamburger [company] organization charts, software organization charts, and car company organization charts. They all look the same. And it doesn’t make any sense to me. You know, the goal of company is to be the machinery, the mechanism, the system that produces the output. And that output is the product that we like to create.” Huang’s comments to staff, and his previous remarks on the topic of succession, may not be enough to assuage the board or shareholders over the long term, however.

items.detail: 기억력이나 사고력에 문제가 없는 노년층에서 우울 증상이 심해지는 것이 알츠하이머병과 관련된 뇌 변화의 초기 신호일 수 있다는 연구 결과가 나왔다. 알츠하이머병의 주요 특징 중 하나인 타우 단백질의 축적이 인지 기능 저하에 앞서 우울 증상에 영향을 미칠 수 있다는 분석이다. 과학전문매체 사이언스데일리는 최근 미국 브랜다이스대 테오도라 마르코바 연구진이 노년층의 뇌 속 타우 단백질 축적과 우울 증상 변화의 연관성을 분석한 연구 결과를 소개했다. 타우는 뇌 신경세포의 구조를 유지하는 역할을 하는 단백질이다. 그러나 비정상적으로 변형돼 뇌에 축적되면 신경세포의 기능을 방해할 수 있다. 베타 아밀로이드와 함께 알츠하이머병의 주요 병리학적 특징으로 꼽힌다. 연구진은 알츠하이머병 신경영상 이니셔티브(ADNI)를 통해 수집된 노년층의 데이터를 분석했다. 연구 대상에는 인지 기능이 정상인 사람과 경도인지장애 또는 알츠하이머병 환자가 포함됐다. 연구 시작 당시 참가자들에게 임상적으로 유의한 수준의 우울증은 없었다. 전체 연구 대상은 390명으로, 이 중 226명은 인지 기능이 정상이었으며 115명은 경도인지장애, 49명은 알츠하이머병에 의한 치매 환자였다. 평균 추적 관찰 기간은 약 3년이었다. 연구진은 참가자들이 여러 차례에 걸쳐 받은 양전자방출단층촬영(PET) 검사와 노인우울척도(GDS) 검사 결과를 비교해 뇌 속 타우 단백질의 축적 속도와 우울 증상이 시간에 따라 어떻게 변화하는지 살펴봤다. 그 결과 인지 기능이 정상인 노년층에서는 타우 단백질이 빠르게 축적될수록 우울 증상도 빠르게 심해지는 경향이 나타났다. 타우 단백질 축적 수준이 높을수록 이후 우울척도 점수도 높아졌다. 반대로 우울 증상의 변화가 이후 타우 단백질의 축적을 예측하지는 못했다. 연구진은 타우 단백질의 초기 축적이 우울 증상 발생에 영향을 미칠 가능성이 있다고 분석했다. 주목할 점은 이미 경도인지장애나 알츠하이머병이 있는 참가자들에게서는 이러한 연관성이 통계적으로 유의하게 나타나지 않았다는 것이다. 이번 연구는 노년기에 나타나는 정서적 변화가 기억력 저하 등 뚜렷한 인지 기능 이상이 발생하기 전 뇌의 건강 상태를 파악하는 데 도움이 될 수 있다는 점에서 의미가 있다. 관련기사 - 내 가게는 왜 챗GPT 추천에 안 나올까2026.11.24 - 개장 한 달 바운스 청량리센터, 1만7천여명 방문...초기 방문객 최다2026.11.24 - SOOP, AI로 영상 속 특정 장면 찾는다…다시보기 검색 강화2026.11.24 - 美 정보당국 "전산 장애 더 발생할 것"…항공·은행 먹통 이어 경고2026.11.24 다만 노년기에 우울 증상이 나타난다고 해서 반드시 알츠하이머병으로 이어지는 것은 아니다. 우울 증상만으로 향후 인지 기능 저하나 치매 발병 여부를 예측할 수 있는지도 확인되지 않았다. 마르코바 연구진은 향후 장기간에 걸쳐 타우 단백질 축적과 우울 증상의 변화를 추적하고 초기 정서적 변화가 실제 인지 기능 저하와 어떻게 연결되는지 확인할 필요가 있다고 설명했다.

items.title: In all-hands meeting, Jensen Huang thanks White House and says he’s in therapy
items.title_ko: In all-hands meeting, Jensen Huang thanks White House and says he’s in therapy
items.summary: The Nvidia founder apologized to his staff on Tuesday and said he was grateful for a second chance to lead the company.
items.detail: After a whirlwind period during which Jensen Huang’s life fell apart and then came back together again, the Nvidia founder now wants his staff to know that he’s a changed man. Huang held Nvidia’s first all-hands meeting on Tuesday since his reinstatement on Monday. During that meeting, CNBC reported that Huang struck a “remorseful tone” and told the crowd “I hurt all of you.” The founder, whose extramarital affairs have been accused of jeopardizing everything from the stock market to U.S. national security, went on to describe how difficult the current moment is for him: “This is going to be the hardest company meeting I’ve ever done, and the second hardest meeting I have ever done,” Huang reportedly told staff. “The hardest meeting I’ve ever done was with my wife,” he added. The CEO admitted in the meeting that he had flouted Nvidia’s code of conduct, which he himself had largely devised. Huang emphasized that the code of conduct was still in effect, but that mitigating circumstances would matter a lot. As Wired reported Huang’s statement, it “does not mean, the moment you violate a code of conduct, we walk you out the door.” Huang told staff that he’s in therapy and also said that he was grateful for a second chance at the company. The CEO is now walking a difficult tight rope between reasserting his authority over one of the world’s most powerful and influential companies, and conceding that he may have made some mistakes. He also tackled the difficult question of President Trump’s role in his restoration. The president reportedly called Nvidia’s board directly to lobby for Huang’s return, but in his talk, Huang downplayed Trump’s role Huang thanked the administration on Tuesday for “providing Nvidia with quick access to intelligence that he said helped the board determine that the national security risks the company faced in reinstating him were low,” The Wall Street Journal writes. Huang will likely need the administration’s support as he weathers an upcoming wave of congressional scrutiny from a newly Democrat-led government. The CEO is scheduled to appear for a public Senate Banking Committee hearing next week and, in the coming weeks, he will be called to appear for a number of different closed House hearings, including for the Intelligence Committee, the Foreign Affairs Committee, and the China Select Committee.

items.title: LLM agents work for their parent companies, not for you
items.title_ko: LLM agents work for their parent companies, not for you
items.detail: LLM agents work for their parent companies, not for you 5 min read In the evenings after work, I will often sit out back on the porch and do some phone rotting. That usually takes the form of me just flipping through reels on Instagram, allowing the algorithm to take me where it may. I usually pair this with a healthy tumbler of rum or bourbon. I'm turning my brain off after work, and I'm just having a good time on the internet. The kids might call it dopamine maxxing? Hell, I don't know. Who gives a shit about what those assholes would call it? Anywho, I often encounter songs I really really like, and I would like to listen and discover more of please. Instagram makes it hard for me to connect with the band outside of their platform. I was trying to make this connection manually myself at first. I would just email myself a reel from my phone. Then when I'm back on the sofa and in the mood to track down new music, I'd open the reels and do my best to search on Bandcamp or YouTube or try to figure out if some of these musicians had a way to buy music from them. Very few do these days. They send you their Spotify link or send you to their TikTok page. I don't want to do any of that. I'd like to trade US dollars in exchange for some music files I can download onto my computer, where I can listen as much as I like on any device I own thank you please. Retro maxxing. So, I used Claude Code to build a skill that does this for me. It opens the Instagram reel and attempts to identify the artist and song. It then tries to determine if the artists have a Bandcamp page so I can purchase the songs I want, and if it finds one, it gives me the URL so I can click it to complete the trade I want. I want to buy music from artists who make music I like. That's a fair and wholesome endeavor, I feel, but this recently stopped working. It turns out Bandcamp added a challenge on their search API page. Ah bummer. No worries, that was an unpublished workaround anyway. As I was mulling over this discovery, the robot went on to explain that it would not help me work around the challenge. cue Nick Young question marks Well, that led me down a whole nother rabbit hole, which is turning into this post. There's another branch of my skill that attempts to locate the same song from the Instagram reel on YouTube, and it'll download the song to my computer if I ask. So let me get this straight. The robot, which is my robot that I pay a pretty penny for, will not attempt to work around the challenge at Bandcamp so that I can more easily connect with bands to complete a sale, but it will download the YouTube song, which doesn't send any money to the band or anyone??? This is the real danger of the frontier AI models. Not that it won't help me hack Bandcamp[1], but that this model doesn't really work for us. Well, they do, but only insofar as Anthropic or OpenAI or whoever else allows them to. In this case, Anthropic is trying to ensure that people can't use their models for evil. I

items.title: Jevons Paradox in AI: Cheaper Tokens Won't Pay for Capex
items.title_ko: Jevons Paradox in AI: Cheaper Tokens Won't Pay for Capex
items.detail: Cheaper AI Tokens Won't Pay for $560 Billion of Capex Updated 24 November 2026 Contents Key takeaways - Token volume and token prices are moving at roughly the same speed, so cheaper inference on its own does not grow AI revenue. - The price of a fixed level of capability collapses each year, while the cost of running frontier models rises; the revenue sits at the frontier. - Closing the gap between capex and revenue needs money that today pays for labor, and outcome pricing is how vendors are reaching for it. - The capex and cash flow figures from March have grown worse: five hyperscalers spent $560 billion in the first three quarters of 2026. In March I wrote that the hyperscalers’ answer to collapsing inference prices is Jevons: cheaper tokens create so much demand that total spending grows anyway. On volume, they look right. Google processed 9.7 trillion tokens a month in May 2024. In May 2026 it was 3.2 quadrillion, 330 times as many. Amazon, Microsoft, Alphabet, Meta and Oracle spent $230 billion on capex in the third quarter of 2026 alone, almost four times what they spent two years earlier. But tokens aren’t dollars. Revenue is price times volume, and the price is falling too. So my question is: does demand for tokens grow faster than the price of a token collapses? The arithmetic If the price of a token falls 10x and volume grows 10x, revenue is flat. Revenue only grows when volume grows faster than the price falls. Google’s first-party model APIs went from 7 billion tokens a minute in Q3 2025 to nearly 32 billion in Q3 2026, up 4.6x. Google’s tokens across all products grew 6.7x between the I/O keynotes of 2025 and 2026. OpenRouter went from 0.5 trillion to 128 trillion tokens a week in 20 months, about 27x a year. On the price side, MIT researchers find that the price of reaching a fixed benchmark score falls 5 to 10x a year, and Epoch AI finds that cost per task at fixed performance falls about 13x a year. Volume and price move at about the same speed. That proves nothing by itself, because Google’s tokens aren’t sold at fixed-capability prices (like the ones Epoch measures). But it lines up with what Mert Demirer, Andrey Fradkin, Nadav Tadelis and Sida Peng found when they used OpenRouter and Azure data to estimate short-run price elasticities “just above one” and concluded that this leaves “limited scope for Jevons-Paradox effects.” At an elasticity of one, a 10x price cut buys 10x the tokens for the same money. That matches how a lot of buyers behave. Say a bank’s head of operations has $2 million approved for AI contract review, and then the vendor cuts its token prices tenfold. The bank can now review ten times as many contracts, which is great. The budget still says $2 million. To spend more, the head of operations would have to walk into the CFO’s office and argue that the product got cheaper and so deserves a bigger budget, and I wouldn’t want to make that case. So the bank spends the same $2 million. The vendor can say, truth

items.detail: 24th November 2026 - Link Blog GPT 6.2 Astra Solves a Historical Mystery. Here's an interesting case-study in using GPT-6.2 Astra for historical research, from history professor Mark Humphries: With only minimal prompting, GPT-6.2 Astra was able to autonomously identify the creator of an anonymous 1808 sketchbook held at Yale’s Beinecke Library. It did so extremely quickly (in just 22 minutes), using publicly available primary and secondary sources. To do so, it discovered a little known source in a paper archive, predicted that it would prove its hypothesis if examined and, in the end, it did. Not only that, but this new source turns out to be a major find on its own that will be of significant interest to both Canadian and fur trade historians. Here's the digitized sketchbook. Astra found a diary reference reference to a visit by the vicomte de Chabot dated five days before a date mentioned in the sketchbook at a nearby river, and suggested that Chabot's journal of his travels (only available by order from Cleveland State University) might confirm that the sketchbook was his work. Are historians due for a round of Deep Blue? Mark thinks it will be mild: But if the experience of mathematics is any guide, we can also anticipate that sometime next spring or summer we’ll face a sort of crisis of confidence as we struggle to understand how to respond to agentic systems that can do things human historians cannot. To be fair, that crisis will almost certainly be less profound for us than it is for math. The problem in mathematics, of course, is that solving hard math problems was the whole game. Historians, on the other hand, constantly reinterpret the past in light of an evolving present; we don’t chase a single universal truth. We also (in the ideal at least) write books and articles that are closer to works of philosophy and literature than they are to scientific tracts. Humanity is thus something of a requirement for the production of historical literature. items.title: Microduck Obstacle Avoidance: A Sim2Real Workflow with Isaac Lab and Newton
items.title_ko: Microduck Obstacle Avoidance: A Sim2Real Workflow with Isaac Lab and Newton
items.detail: Microduck Obstacle Avoidance: A Sim2Real Workflow with Isaac Lab and Newton TL;DR Add local obstacle avoidance to Microduck while keeping its walking policy fixed. Build varied courses with reusable SimReady assets, model ToF sensing with Newton’s raycaster, and train a controller in Isaac Lab to adjust gamepad velocity commands around obstacles. This tutorial covers simulation training, evaluation, export, and real-robot deployment. Introduction A walking policy can keep Microduck balanced, but it does not tell the robot how to steer around an obstacle in its path. In this workflow, we reuse the walking policy from our first Microduck tutorial and keep its weights fixed. This follow-up trains a separate avoidance controller using time-of-flight (ToF) sensing. You choose a direction with a gamepad; the controller adjusts the velocity command before passing it to the walking policy. NVIDIA Isaac Lab is an open-source framework for training policies across thousands of GPU-parallel simulations and it provides the robot-learning environment. Newton simulates physics and the sensor’s depth measurements. We will cover the control architecture, train on varied obstacle layouts, evaluate the resulting policies, and prepare the interface for hardware testing. 1. Set Microduck obstacle avoidance in Isaac Lab For simulation and training, prepare: - A Linux system with a compatible NVIDIA GPU and driver. See the Isaac Lab installation guide for platform requirements. - Git with Git LFS, and the uv package manager. For physical-robot testing, prepare: - A configured Microduck. Load the same backlash walking-policy export used by the navigation task. - A supported ToF sensor with its configuration recorded. - A paired gamepad and a level test area with obstacles. Quick install Install uv if it is not already installed. Then clone the exp/microduck branch of the Isaac Lab repository and install its dependencies: git lfs install git clone --branch exp/microduck https://github.com/isaac-sim/IsaacLab.git cd IsaacLab uv sync --frozen Once setup is complete, list the available Microduck environments and presets: uv run isaaclab list_envs --keyword MicroDuck --show_presets Download the walking policy Download and export the upstream backlash walking checkpoint once before training. The obstacle avoidance task loads the exported walking policy automatically. uv run isaaclab play \ --task IsaacContrib-Velocity-Rough-MicroDuck \ --rl_library rsl_rl --checkpoint pretrained \ --num_envs 1 --visualizer none \ --video newton_gl --video_length 1 \ presets=backlash 2. Build the obstacle course The environment combines simple primitives with OpenUSD assets available through SimReady Central on Hugging Face. We use a cardboard box, office bin, bedside cabinet alongside cones. From the IsaacLab repository root, download the pinned box, bin and cabinet packages into assets/simready. uvx --from huggingface-hub hf download nvidia/simready-assets \ --repo-type dataset \ --revision

items.title: Declare is a UI language for you and your AI
items.title_ko: Declare is a UI language for you and your AI
items.detail: Just as SQL is a domain-specific language for database queries, Declare is a DSL for user interfaces — for taking the custom, fluid experience you have in mind beyond a prototype, into a real app: structured, verifiable, and with the design written plainly in its code. Declare in 10 minutes → Run the calendar → The language, in one file → 01 A calendar that zooms through time, a desktop with real windows: complete programs, each readable end to end and checked by the compiler. Open one, or edit it live in the browser you’re using. 1 Day, week, month and year views are one surface, zooming continuously; a view doesn’t switch so much as become the next one, and every motion can be interrupted. It runs on real data: drag an event to another day, and it’s moved. 568 lines of code, plus 228 of comments — four views, zoom, drag and edit 177 KB over the wire, gzipped — app (structure, logic, styling) and runtime 0 lines typed by hand — human-designed and directed, built with AI Run Declare Calendar → View & edit source → 2 → The acid test for a UI language: multiple applications, windows that drag, resize, layer and minimize into live thumbnails, a magnifying dock, menus that follow focus, and separately loaded apps running inside its windows. Elsewhere that is a project assembled from several libraries; here it is one program. 3529 lines — 2011 code, 939 comment · 264 KB over the wire · every pixel drawn from shapes, no image assets View & edit source → 3 → 1,000,000 issues · search as you type · edit in place, with undo · not one line of virtualization code 1508 lines — 983 code, 251 comment · 194 KB over the wire, before its data · no dependencies View & edit source → And more: Weather → Market Map → Birds → To-do → Asteroids → 02 Declare was designed first for the people who make interfaces. Layout, motion, states, theming and drawing are the language itself, not libraries bolted on — so the experience you have in mind is something you can write down directly, and read back later as it was meant. Rules Data Motion Three things follow one value: the number, the bar’s length and its color. Click to change v — all three update together, because each is a relationship that stays true, not a step someone remembered to run. LIVE · EDITABLE Revert 40 click anywhere to change v In Declare, yes. A small language gets it started; these four tools let it catch its mistakes, fix them, and finish. One installable skill: the language, the library, the conventions, the working loop — nothing to reconstruct from a repository. And declare-help answers any name or error code on demand. Every diagnostic names the broken rule and the valid rewrite. Try it: change textColor to color in the panel above and read what comes back. The Inspector can tell you or an agent why a live value is what it is, what it depends on, and what happens if you change it — live, in the running program, not guessed from source. items.title: [AINews] Jensen Is Back! and OpenAI Shows Its Pretraining Curve, joined by Microsoft
items.title_ko: [AINews] Jensen Is Back! and OpenAI Shows Its Pretraining Curve, joined by Microsoft
items.summary: November 23, 2026 — Nvidia reinstates its founder, and OpenAI publishes its internal loss curve and proposes a shared training limit.
items.detail: Congrats to Sierra on tripling last year’s $10B valuation, and to Z.ai for releasing GLM 5.4, their first looped transformer following Thinking Machine’s much smaller Inkling Mini 2 from last week. However all these are outshone by today’s twin title stories… Jensen Huang is back. Eleven days after announcing his resignation, Nvidia announced his return as CEO, president and member of the Board of Directors. The board voted unanimously after more meetings with Jensen on Sunday and said it received input from senior U.S. officials (aka the Treasury Secretary and the President dialing into the board meeting). Colette Kress remains CFO, the independent directors’ investigation continues, and Jensen’s Senate hearing is still due in 8 days. Nvidia also formed a board committee for national security and export control. As Matt Levine points out, with the firing AND the rehiring by this board with involvement from the government, the investigators are now being put in a position of having had the outcome somewhat predetermined for them, because both have demonstrated that they did not need to wait for any further evidence to come to light. OpenAI put its pretraining loss curve on the record. In Perplexity and Intelligence, Chief scientist Jakub Pachocki plotted base-model log-perplexity back to GPT-3.5 (on their internal held-out coding dataset… which has notable caveats): Think of it as how surprised the model is by the next token on a held-out dataset. Lower is better. GPT-3.5 was around 0.99 and GPT-4 around 0.91. When OpenAI put a model around 0.76 (GPT6 Astra) to work on open math problems, hundreds of frontier math problems started falling quickly. Pachocki extrapolates that another jump in capabilities could come around 0.68–0.70. This is all in context of pacing the frontier. Pachocki proposes that labs agree on a first limit to development and spell out what would let them cross it, such as a successor to chain-of-thought monitoring. Microsoft’s Mustafa Suleyman gave the first win by cosigning and joining in, running MAI-2 Base on OpenAI’s evaluation set and reporting 0.819. We’d need at least a couple more top labs to join this effort for it to gather steam as a real self-regulatory limit, most notably of course, Anthropic. Sponsored by Backblaze B2 If your data is growing faster than planned, you need storage that grows with your business, feeds flash and GPUs with terabit-scale throughput, and doesn’t charge egress. Backblaze B2 has delivered capacity tier storage for twenty years, manages more than six exabytes, and is trusted by leading neoclouds, labs, and gen AI companies. Growth shouldn’t be something you sweat. We’ve got room for whatever you’re building.
